newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY WELCOMES US NATO SUPPORT.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY WELCOMES US NATO SUPPORT.

text.p: Hungary on Thursday welcomed the U.S.'s message to its NATO allies that Washington favoured inviting Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic into the alliance next month but insisted enlargement must continue to include other east European states.

"This is a major step," Hungarian foreign ministry spokesman Gabor Szentivanyi told Reuters. "This decision further strengthens us in our expectations that the NATO summit im Madrid will make a favourable decision regarding Hungary's invitation to the alliance.
"We fully agree with the strong emphasis the (United States) put on leaving the doors open for further new members and that no-one should be excluded from consideration for membership.

Secretary of State William Cohen presented the U.S. position to a meeting of NATO defence ministers, their last session before a summit in Madrid on July 8-9 at which some of NATO's former enemies from communist Europe will be invited to join.

A NATO source present at the meeting said the announcement by the U.S., by far NATO's most important member, had clearly shocked some other member states. France in particular had pushed for a broader enlargement to include Romania and possibly Slovenia.

Earlier on Thursday White House spokesman Mike McCurry said in Washington that the U.S. position was firm. Asked if the U.S. might be over-ruled on the matter he replied "That is not likely". NATO operates by consensus and the U.S. position is backed by several other countries.
Szentivanyi said that while Hungary feels it should now qualify for the first round of admission it was in Hungary's interest that as many of its neighbours should qualify for membership as possible.

During its long campaign to be considered for early NATO adhesion Hungary has concluded basic treaties with all its neighbours ending decades of tension over boundaries and the status of ethnic Hungarians, notably in Slovakia and Romania.

While Slovakia dropped out of contention for early NATO membership after international criticism of its slow rate of reform, Romania has given itself an outside chance of being in the first round since its new reformist government was elected last November.

One of the the main priorities of new Romanian president Emil Constantinescu has been to improve relations with Hungary through a string of bilateral accords on military and political cooperation signed earlier this year.
Szentivanyi denied that if Romania were not admitted to NATO in the first wave new tensions would appear between Budapest amnd Bucharest.
"I think the relationship (with Romania) is based on firm principles and on a very wide range of economic political and military exchanges.
"There is trust between the two countries and I believe Hungary will do its best to increase cooperation and through this help Romania's aspirations," he said.
